selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh-squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Desert Camp in the Sahara
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga, watching the sunset paint the sand in fiery hues. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a sky blazing with stars, enjoy a tagine dinner around a campfire, and wake up for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Wander the Ancient Medina and Souks
experiences.description: Get lost in the labyrinthine alleyways of Marrakech's 11th-century Medina, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Discover artisan workshops crafting leather, ceramics, and metalwork. Bargain for spices, lanterns, and handwoven rugs in the vibrant souks of Souk Semmarine and Souk el-Attarine.

experiences.name: Visit the Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a visit to the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, featuring intricate zellij tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Then explore the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, adorned with exquisite Moorish craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Sandboarding on the Sahara Dunes
experiences.description: Strap on a board and carve your way down the towering golden dunes of Erg Chebbi for an adrenaline-pumping desert adventure. Local guides provide boards and instruction, making it accessible for beginners and thrilling for experienced riders. Combine with quad biking across the desert floor for the ultimate Sahara adventure day.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~50-80 MAD) or shared airport shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or hotel reception if available. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from hotel or nearby convenience store upon arrival (~20-30 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night — no sightseeing planned. Confirm hotel has 24-hour reception for late check-in. Keep small change in Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) ready for the taxi. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM upon arrival for best rates.

day_by_day.morning: After a good rest, enjoy a budget breakfast near the hotel, then head to the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square — the beating heart of Marrakech. Arrive early to explore the square while it's calm and atmospheric. Walk through the surrounding souks (markets) of the Medina: Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices (spice market), and the dyers' quarter. Bargain respectfully for souvenirs. Entrance to the souks is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior, free) and then head to the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD entry), a beautiful 19th-century palace with intricate Moroccan tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, stroll through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Bab Agnaou gate — all free to walk through.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air carnival with snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Grab dinner from the famous food stalls in the square — one of the best budget experiences in Morocco. Try harira soup, merguez sandwiches, or grilled kefta.

meals.breakfast: Café de France or a local café near Djemaa el-Fna — mint tea, msemen (flatbread), and amlou (almond-argan dip) for ~30-40 MAD
meals.lunch: Street food in the souks — a bowl of harira soup and bread for ~15-25 MAD, or a fresh-squeezed orange juice (5 MAD) and a sandwich
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — full grilled meal with kefta, salad, and bread for ~50-80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina's narrow alleys involve a lot of walking. Beware of unofficial 'guides' who may try to lead you into shops for commission. Carry a small daypack and keep valuables secure in crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD entry) — a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring beautifully decorated mausoleums. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Afterward, walk to the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now in atmospheric ruins with rooftop views over Marrakech and storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Majorelle Garden (~150 MAD entry, or ~200 MAD including the Berber Museum inside) — a magical cobalt-blue garden created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Budget tip: if the entry feels steep, the exterior walls and the surrounding Gueliz neighborhood are free to explore. Alternatively, visit the free Cyber Park nearby for a relaxing green space. Then explore the Gueliz (New City) neighborhood for a change of pace.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free rooftop sunset view from one of Marrakech's café terraces overlooking Djemaa el-Fna (many cafés allow you to sit with just a drink purchase). Enjoy the call to prayer echoing across the Medina at dusk. Spend the evening wandering the lantern-lit souks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local bakery (hanout) near the Medina — fresh bread, olive oil, and coffee for ~20-30 MAD
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant near El Badi Palace — a set menu (menu du jour) with tagine, salad, and bread for ~60-80 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad restaurant in the Medina or a local eatery — couscous or tagine for ~60-100 MAD. Try Restaurant Haj Brik near Djemaa el-Fna for authentic, affordable Moroccan food

day_by_day.notes: The Majorelle Garden can be crowded midday — visit later in the afternoon for better photos. Student discounts may be available at some sites with valid ID. Combine the Saadian Tombs and El Badi Palace in one morning as they are within walking distance of each other.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 06:00-07:00) from Marrakech on a budget shared minibus or CTM/Supratours bus toward Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley — the gateway to the Sahara. Book in advance (~80-150 MAD one way). The journey crosses the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at a roadside Berber café for tea with panoramic mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ouarzazate (~4 hours). Visit the impressive Kasbah Taourirt (~20 MAD entry) — a massive 20th-century earthen fortress and UNESCO-listed site. Walk through the adjacent UNESCO-protected Ksar (fortified village). Explore the Ouarzazate film studios area (exterior is free to view) — Morocco's 'Hollywood of the desert' used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.evening: Continue by shared transport or pre-arranged budget group tour (~150-200 MAD extra) toward Zagora or M'Hamid — the edge of the Sahara Desert. Check into a budget desert guesthouse or auberge (~150-250 MAD per night). Enjoy a simple Berber dinner under a spectacular star-filled desert sky.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — bread, jam, and coffee, or grab a pastry from a bakery near the bus station (~20-30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber café in the Atlas Mountains or Ouarzazate — tagine and mint tea for ~50-70 MAD
meals.dinner: Guesthouse-cooked Berber meal — traditional tagine or couscous with vegetables (~60-80 MAD, often included in guesthouse package)

day_by_day.notes: Book shared transport or a budget group tour in advance from Marrakech — many hostels and budget travel agencies in Djemaa el-Fna area offer affordable 2-3 day Sahara packages for ~800-1,200 MAD including transport, accommodation, and camel ride. This is often the most budget-friendly option. The mountain road can be winding — take motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) for a magical camel trek into the Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes (depending on your location). Watch the sunrise paint the golden dunes in shades of orange and pink — one of Morocco's most spectacular sights. A 1-2 hour camel ride costs approximately ~150-250 MAD per person. Climb the highest dune on foot for panoramic desert views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the guesthouse for a late breakfast or early lunch. Spend the afternoon exploring the desert on foot or by quad bike (optional, ~150-200 MAD/hour). Visit a local Berber nomad camp to learn about traditional desert life, drink tea, and see handmade crafts. Rest during the hottest part of the day in the shade of your guesthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Optional: spend the night in a budget desert camp (bivouac) under the stars — many guesthouses offer this for ~200-300 MAD including dinner and breakfast. Enjoy traditional Berber music around a campfire, stargazing in one of the darkest skies in North Africa, and the profound silence of the Sahara at night.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-sunrise snack (dates and water) before camel trek, then full Berber breakfast at guesthouse after returning (~included or ~30-40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Guesthouse lunch — Moroccan salad, bread, and tagine (~50-70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Desert camp dinner — traditional Berber couscous or tagine cooked over fire (~included in camp package or ~80-100 MAD separately)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headscarf or bandana to protect against sand and sun. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and a refillable water bottle are essential. Temperatures in March are pleasant during the day (~20-25°C) but can drop significantly at night (~5-10°C) — bring a warm layer. Bargain politely for camel rides and quad bikes.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from the desert back toward Marrakech via the scenic Draa Valley route. Stop at the ancient fortified village of Aït Benhaddou (~10 MAD entry to the ksar interior) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Morocco's most photogenic kasbahs, used as a filming location for countless movies and TV series. Explore the labyrinthine earthen towers and enjoy views over the valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey back through the High Atlas Mountains. Optional stop at the Tizi n'Tichka pass for photos. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back into your hotel, shower, and rest. Take a gentle evening stroll through the quieter parts of the Medina to decompress after the desert adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Marrakech Museum (Musée de Marrakech, ~50 MAD) housed in the beautiful 19th-century Mnebhi Palace — free for the last hour before closing at some times. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed hammam experience at a local public hammam (not a tourist spa) for as little as ~15-30 MAD — an authentic Moroccan cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Desert camp or guesthouse breakfast before departure — bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea (~included or ~30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at Aït Benhaddou or Ouarzazate — sandwiches or a quick tagine at a local café (~40-60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — treat yourself to a slightly nicer sit-down Moroccan restaurant for your last full Marrakech evening. Try Café Clock or a local riad restaurant for a memorable meal (~80-120 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Aït Benhaddou is a must-see — allow at least 1.5-2 hours to explore properly. The return journey from the desert to Marrakech is approximately 6-8 hours total with stops. If using a group tour package, transport back is typically included. Confirm your return transport the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final morning in Marrakech. Head back to the souks for any last-minute souvenir shopping — great budget buys include argan oil, Moroccan spices (ras el hanout, cumin), leather goods, handmade pottery, and woven textiles. Practice your bargaining skills one last time! Visit any sites you may have missed earlier in the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final mint tea and pastry at a café terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna. Pack your bags and check out of the hotel. Take a petit taxi to Marrakech Menara Airport (~50-80 MAD). Arrive at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Browse the duty-free shops for any final Moroccan souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech with incredible memories of the Medina's labyrinthine souks, the High Atlas Mountains, and the golden dunes of the Sahara Desert.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a local café — mint tea, msemen, honey, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~30-40 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or airport — a sandwich or pastry (~20-40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 7 days (excluding flights and hotel): Entrance fees ~500-600 MAD, Transport ~500-700 MAD, Meals ~1,000-1,400 MAD, Desert experience ~500-800 MAD, Souvenirs ~200-500 MAD. Total approximate spend: ~2,700-4,000 MAD (~$270-400 USD) for the week, making this a very achievable budget trip. Exchange any leftover Dirhams at the airport before departure as MAD is a restricted currency and difficult to exchange abroad.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Pre-arranged airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and unwind. If hungry, enjoy a light late-night snack at the hotel's lounge or bar.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at layover airport
meals.dinner: Light hotel lounge snack upon late arrival — hummus, flatbread, mint tea (approx. 80–120 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Given the 22:30 arrival, keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm hotel transfer in advance. Exchange some currency at the airport (ATMs available). Rest well — big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. After breakfast, head to Jemaa el-Fna Square — the beating heart of Marrakech. Explore the open-air spectacle of storytellers, musicians, and snake charmers. Wander into the adjacent souks (markets) of Souk Semmarine for spices, leather goods, and Moroccan lanterns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with intricate tilework and painted ceilings. Afterward, explore the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues. Stop at the Ben Youssef Madrasa — one of North Africa's largest Islamic schools — for its breathtaking courtyard (entrance ~70 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at dusk when the square transforms into a massive open-air food festival. Dine at one of the rooftop terraces overlooking the square — try Café de France or Le Grand Balcon du Café Glacier for atmospheric views. Enjoy a traditional Moroccan dinner with a glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice.

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet breakfast — pastries, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), eggs, mint tea
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Jemaa el-Fna — harira soup, kefta sandwich, fresh-squeezed OJ (80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant dinner — lamb tagine or bastilla (pigeon pie), Moroccan salad (150–220 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Bargaining is expected in the souks — start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep small change handy for photos with performers. Dress modestly out of respect for local culture.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Saadian Tombs — a hidden necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring elaborate royal burial chambers (entrance ~70 MAD). Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins, a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now an evocative open-air ruin with storks nesting on its walls (entrance ~70 MAD). Climb the ramparts for panoramic views of the medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a taxi or guided tour to the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~150 MAD) — a vivid cobalt-blue botanical garden originally designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Visit the adjacent Berber Museum on-site. Afterward, explore the Gueliz neighborhood (Marrakech's modern French-designed district) for contemporary art galleries and boutique shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Moroccan hammam (steam bath) for relaxation and cultural immersion. Many mid-range hammams offer a scrub-and-massage package for 200–350 MAD (try Hammam de la Rose or similar). Afterward, dine at a riad restaurant in the medina for an intimate Moroccan feast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café — amlou (almond-argan dip) with bread, coffee (60–90 MAD if eating out)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Gueliz at a modern café — Moroccan-fusion salad, sandwich, fresh juice (100–150 MAD)
meals.dinner: Riad restaurant dinner — slow-cooked lamb mechoui or chicken with preserved lemon tagine, Moroccan mint tea (180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance, especially in peak season. Majorelle Garden can get crowded after 10am — arrive early if possible. The Gueliz area is great for picking up quality souvenirs at more fixed (and fair) prices.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (around 7:00–8:00am) by private or shared transfer for the epic drive to the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley and Dadès Gorge — a full-day journey of approximately 8–9 hours with scenic stops. Pass through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) — stunning mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the UNESCO-listed Ksar of Aït Benhaddou — a spectacular fortified mud-brick village used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia (entrance ~10 MAD). Explore the ancient ksar on foot and cross the riverbed. Continue driving through the Valley of Roses and Dadès Gorge, arriving in the Merzouga/Erfoud area by late afternoon or early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp or Merzouga guesthouse near the Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount camels for a sunset camel trek into the Sahara (1–1.5 hours, included with most desert camp packages or ~200–300 MAD separately). Watch the sunset over the golden dunes — one of Morocco's most iconic experiences. Overnight in a mid-range desert camp with private tents.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — bread, cheese, eggs, coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou — tagine or couscous at a local restaurant (80–130 MAD)
meals.dinner: Desert camp dinner under the stars — traditional Berber meal of couscous, tagine, Moroccan salads, mint tea (usually included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — bring water, snacks, sunscreen, and a light jacket (mountain passes can be cold in March). Book your desert camp in advance. Mid-range camps offer private Berber-style tents with en-suite bathrooms. The camel ride at sunset is unmissable.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (around 5:30am) for a magical sunrise over the Erg Chebbi dunes — the shifting colors from deep orange to gold are extraordinary. Optional: climb the highest dune on foot for panoramic views (30–45 min hike). After sunrise, enjoy a Berber breakfast at camp. For the adventurous, try sandboarding down the dunes (boards available at camp or nearby rental, ~50–100 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby village of Merzouga to interact with local Berber families. Optional: explore the Gnawa musicians' neighborhood or visit a fossil and mineral shop (the region is rich in prehistoric marine fossils). In the afternoon, begin the return journey westward, stopping at the Todra Gorge — a dramatic narrow canyon with 300-meter-high rock walls, perfect for a short hike or scramble along the riverbed.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a mid-range guesthouse or kasbah hotel in the Boumalne Dadès or Tinghir area. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the guesthouse or a local restaurant. Stargaze from the terrace — the skies in this remote region are exceptionally clear.

meals.breakfast: Desert camp Berber breakfast — khobz bread, amlou, olive oil, honey, mint tea (included in camp)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from camp or roadside stop near Merzouga — sandwiches, fruit, water
meals.dinner: Guesthouse or local restaurant dinner — beef or vegetable tagine with Moroccan bread (100–160 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a warm layer for the pre-dawn dune climb — March desert nights are cold (can drop to 5–10°C). Sunrise is typically around 6:30–7:00am in mid-March. Stay hydrated throughout the day. Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the morning light but still beautiful in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Drive through the spectacular Dadès Gorge — often called the 'Road of a Thousand Kasbahs' — with its winding mountain roads and ancient mud-brick fortresses. Stop for photos at the famous curved road viewpoint. Continue west through the Draa Valley palm groves toward Ouarzazate — Morocco's 'Hollywood of Africa.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ouarzazate: visit the Taourirt Kasbah (entrance ~20 MAD), a sprawling UNESCO-listed mud-brick palace. Optionally visit the Atlas Film Studios (entrance ~60 MAD) — one of the world's largest film studios where scenes from dozens of international productions were filmed. Browse local shops for handmade Berber rugs and silver jewelry. Begin the return drive toward Marrakech over the High Atlas via Tizi n'Tichka pass.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (approximately 6:00–7:00pm). Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a final evening in Marrakech — visit a rooftop bar for cocktails (try a non-alcoholic Moroccan cocktail with rose water and citrus), then stroll through the illuminated medina at night for a final atmospheric experience.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ouarzazate at a local café — mixed Moroccan salads, tagine, mint tea (90–140 MAD)
meals.dinner: Marrakech restaurant dinner — celebrate the return with a proper Moroccan feast; try pastilla (sweet-savory pigeon or chicken pie) and a fresh fruit dessert (180–250 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Dadès Gorge road can be narrow and winding — take it slow and enjoy the scenery. Fill up on fuel in Ouarzazate before the mountain pass. If driving yourself, ensure the vehicle has good tires for the mountain roads. The Tizi n'Tichka pass may have snow patches in March — check conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Marrakech. Enjoy a slow hotel breakfast. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entrance ~50 MAD) housed in a stunning 19th-century palace — excellent collection of Moroccan art, ceramics, and manuscripts. Alternatively, spend the morning doing final souvenir shopping in the souks — argan oil products, leather poufs, Moroccan slippers (babouches), and spice blends make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a farewell lunch at a traditional Moroccan restaurant. Spend the remaining afternoon relaxing at the hotel pool or getting a final massage/treatment. Pack and prepare for departure. Arrange airport transfer (approximately 15–20 minutes from the medina area to the airport).
day_by_day.evening: Depart for Marrakech Menara Airport for your onward flight. Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Enjoy a final mint tea at the airport and reflect on an incredible Moroccan adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel buffet breakfast — enjoy a full spread of Moroccan and continental options
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a traditional Moroccan restaurant — couscous (traditionally served on Fridays in Morocco), harira soup, Moroccan pastries for dessert (150–200 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or light snack before departure — Moroccan airport cafés offer sandwiches and mint tea (80–120 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some MAD for last-minute purchases or tips. Tipping is customary in Morocco: 10–15 MAD for porters, 20–50 MAD for guides, 10% of the bill for restaurant staff. Ensure all purchased goods (especially argan oil) are properly sealed for air travel. Check airline liquid restrictions. Keep your passport and boarding pass easily accessible.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Private airport transfer in a luxury vehicle to Aegean Bliss Resort in Marrakech. Upon arrival, enjoy a traditional Moroccan welcome with mint tea and rose water. Check in to your beachfront suite, unwind with a light nightcap at the hotel's rooftop lounge, and prepare for the adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome mezze platter and Moroccan pastries arranged by the hotel upon arrival – light bites served in your suite or at the lounge bar

day_by_day.notes: Arrange for a pre-booked private transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK). Confirm arrival with the hotel concierge in advance so a dedicated butler is ready. Keep Day 1 light – rest is essential before a packed itinerary begins.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast, embark on a private guided tour of the UNESCO-listed Marrakech Medina. Explore the 12th-century Koutoubia Mosque (exterior), the ornate Bahia Palace, and the hauntingly beautiful El Badi Palace ruins. Your expert guide will provide rich historical context about the Saadian dynasty and Almoravid architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the exquisite Saadian Tombs, then meander through the vibrant souks of the Medina – spice markets, leather tanneries viewed from rooftop terraces, and artisan workshops. Enjoy a private shopping experience with a personal stylist guide to select authentic Moroccan crafts, lanterns, and textiles without the hassle of bargaining.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop terrace of a historic riad in the Medina, followed by a private dinner at La Mamounia's Le Marocain restaurant – one of Morocco's most celebrated fine-dining establishments featuring live traditional Gnawa music and a curated menu of bastilla, lamb tagine, and couscous royale.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Moroccan breakfast spread at Aegean Bliss Resort – msemen flatbreads, argan oil honey, fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan pastries, and eggs to order
meals.lunch: Rooftop lunch at Nomad Restaurant in the Medina – modern Moroccan cuisine with panoramic views of the souks; try the lamb kefta tacos and preserved lemon chicken
meals.dinner: Private dinner at Le Marocain, La Mamounia – prix-fixe tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. 150–200 EUR per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book La Mamounia dinner well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina – streets are cobblestone and narrow. A private guide is strongly recommended to navigate the labyrinthine souks efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Majorelle Garden – the iconic cobalt-blue botanical masterpiece co-owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Follow with a tour of the adjacent Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech (MYSLM), showcasing the legendary designer's Moroccan-inspired collections and archives. Arrive early for a serene, crowd-free experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a 3-hour Royal Hammam & Spa ritual at the hotel's luxury spa or at a premium traditional hammam such as Hammam de la Rose – includes black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, argan oil massage, and rose petal bath. Spend the remaining afternoon at leisure by the resort pool.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Fantasia show (Tbourida) experience at a luxury equestrian estate outside Marrakech – a spectacular display of Berber horsemanship and traditional music. Followed by a candlelit dinner under the stars in a private desert-style tent with live oud music.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast with fresh fruit platters, Moroccan crepes, and specialty coffees delivered by your personal butler
meals.lunch: Light post-hammam lunch at Café de la Poste – a colonial-era brasserie serving refined Moroccan-French fusion; try the duck pastilla and citrus salad
meals.dinner: Private tented dinner at the Fantasia estate – traditional Moroccan feast including harira soup, mechoui slow-roasted lamb, and chebakia pastries with mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: The Majorelle Garden can get busy after 10 AM – aim to arrive at opening (8 AM). Book the Fantasia experience through the hotel concierge as a private exclusive event. Hammam should be pre-booked 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private 4x4 luxury vehicle for a scenic drive through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation). Stop at panoramic viewpoints and visit a traditional Berber village where you'll be welcomed into a local family's home for an authentic cultural exchange and insight into Amazigh (Berber) life and traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the dramatic Ourika Valley – hike to the picturesque Setti Fatma waterfalls with your private guide (moderate 45-minute trail). Alternatively, opt for a mule trek along the valley for a more adventurous experience. Visit a women's argan oil cooperative to learn about the traditional extraction process.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marrakech by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort – sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar followed by an intimate dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant. Early rest recommended before the Sahara journey tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the resort before departure – eggs, Moroccan bread, fresh juices, and yogurt
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber tagine lunch at a family-run mountain auberge in the Ourika Valley – slow-cooked lamb with prunes and almonds, fresh bread, and mint tea served on a terrace overlooking the valley
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant – contemporary Moroccan cuisine; try the sea bass chermoula and pistachio-stuffed dates for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Tizi n'Tichka pass road can be winding – those prone to motion sickness should take precautions. Dress in layers as mountain temperatures can be significantly cooler than Marrakech. Confirm 4x4 private transfer the night before.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – March 19 (Journey to the Sahara – Merzouga)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort after breakfast. Begin the iconic overland journey to the Sahara Desert via private luxury 4x4. Drive through the dramatic Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and the rose-growing town of Kelaat M'Gouna. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou – a breathtaking fortified ksar used as a backdrop for Game of Thrones and Gladiator – for a private guided tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') with a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios. Pass through the Todgha Gorge for a short scenic walk through the towering canyon walls (300m high). Continue toward Erfoud and Merzouga as the landscape transforms into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara at golden hour. Mount your private camel caravan and ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes as the sun sets over the sea of sand. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp – a private tented suite with en-suite bathroom, plush bedding, and handcrafted Moroccan furnishings. Enjoy stargazing with a telescope, traditional Gnawa music performance around a bonfire, and a sumptuous desert feast.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – full Moroccan spread with pastries and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a luxury riad restaurant in Ouarzazate – Moroccan salads, kefta brochettes, and fresh-pressed pomegranate juice
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the luxury desert camp – Moroccan mezze spread, slow-roasted mechoui lamb, vegetable couscous, and traditional sweets under a canopy of stars

day_by_day.notes: The full overland drive is approximately 8–9 hours with stops – an early departure (7:30 AM) is essential. Alternatively, consider a private charter flight from Marrakech to Ouarzazate to reduce travel time (check availability with concierge). Pack a light jacket as desert nights in March can drop to 10–12°C. Confirm luxury camp booking well in advance as exclusive tents are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for a private sunrise hot air balloon flight over the Erg Chebbi dunes – a truly once-in-a-lifetime perspective of the Sahara as the first light paints the sand in shades of gold and amber. Upon landing, enjoy a Champagne breakfast in the dunes. Return to camp for a traditional Moroccan breakfast and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Choose your Sahara adventure: opt for a thrilling private sandboarding session on the towering dunes, a guided quad biking excursion through the desert landscape, or a meditative solo camel ride with your personal guide. Visit a nomadic Berber family encampment for an authentic cultural exchange – learn about traditional desert navigation, medicinal plants, and nomadic crafts. Enjoy a relaxed siesta during the hottest part of the afternoon at the camp.
day_by_day.evening: As temperatures cool, hike to the summit of a high dune for a private sunset viewing with Champagne and Moroccan canapés prepared by your camp chef. Return to camp for a traditional music and storytelling session around the fire with local Gnawa musicians. Enjoy your final night under the most spectacular star-filled sky you may ever witness.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in the dunes post-balloon flight, followed by a full Moroccan breakfast at camp – msemen, honey, argan oil, fresh fruit, and Berber whiskey (mint tea)
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at the camp – mezze of zaalouk, taktouka, fresh bread, grilled meats, and seasonal vegetables
meals.dinner: Gala desert dinner at the camp – a multi-course Moroccan feast with bastilla au poulet, lamb tagine with apricots, saffron couscous, and pastilla au lait for dessert, paired with Moroccan wines

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon flights are weather-dependent – have a backup sunrise dune hike planned. Apply high-SPF sunscreen as desert sun is intense even in March. Sandstorms are rare in March but carry a light scarf/shemagh for face protection. Quad biking requires a valid driver's license.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk in the dunes before departing the desert camp. Private 4x4 transfer back toward Marrakech, stopping at the spectacular Todgha Gorge for a final photo opportunity and a short walk. Continue through the scenic Valley of Roses and the Skoura palm grove oasis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech in the early afternoon. Freshen up at a luxury day-use suite (pre-arranged by concierge). Spend the final hours exploring the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter), visiting the Mouassine Fountain, and picking up last-minute souvenirs from a curated artisan boutique with your personal shopping guide. Visit the legendary Djemaa el-Fna square – the beating heart of Marrakech – to soak in the atmosphere of storytellers, musicians, and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Dar Yacout or Le Tobsil – two of Marrakech's most atmospheric and exclusive traditional riads, offering a royal Moroccan feast in a candlelit courtyard setting. Private airport transfer departs for your onward journey, closing an unforgettable 7-day Moroccan adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast in the Sahara – dates, fresh bread, Berber omelette, and mint tea as the desert sun rises
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic roadside auberge en route – harira soup, Moroccan salads, and grilled brochettes
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Dar Yacout – prix-fixe royal Moroccan banquet including pastilla, three tagine varieties, couscous, and traditional dessert spread with live Andalusian music (reservations essential, approx. 80–120 EUR per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and arrange airport transfer timing with hotel concierge. Dar Yacout requires advance reservations – book at least 3–4 days prior. Allow extra time at Djemaa el-Fna as the atmosphere is magnetic and easy to lose track of time. Tip your private guides and camp staff generously – 10–15% is customary for premium services in Morocco.
